name: Hypomyelination Neuropathy-Arthrogryposis Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Hypomyelination Neuropathy with Joint Contractures

criteria.description: Presence of congenital arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with distal joint contractures
Evidence of peripheral neuropathy with hypomyelination on nerve conduction studies and nerve biopsy
MRI demonstrating diffuse hypomyelination in central and peripheral nervous system
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with hypomyelination neuropathies (e.g., FAM126A mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital arthrogryposis with neuropathy confirmed by electrophysiology or biopsy and characteristic hypomyelination on MRI
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical and electrophysiological findings are essential.

laboratory: Nerve conduction studies showing reduced conduction velocity consistent with hypomyelination
Nerve biopsy demonstrating hypomyelination and onion bulb formations
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord showing diffuse hypomyelination
Musculoskeletal imaging revealing joint contractures and deformities
other: Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with more severe motor impairment

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness in infancy
Severe respiratory compromise due to neuromuscular weakness
Loss of deep tendon reflexes with joint contractures
references: Kleopa KA, et al. Hypomyelinating neuropathies: clinical and genetic aspects. Neurol Clin. 2012.
Timmerman V, et al. Hereditary neuropathies: molecular genetics and clinical implications. Nat Rev Neurol. 2014.
